observed_native_failure: grow has fully constructed replacement storage before destroying old slots in ascending order. A throwing destructor ends that slot lifetime, stops destruction, keeps original receiver Size/Capacity/Data, and abandons the completed replacement allocation. Failed reconstruction similarly leaves an uninitialized slot and preserves earlier repaired slots.
safe_baseline: Current reserve_with_relocation is intentionally retained: old Drop panic destroys remaining old values and publishes replacement capacity/storage through Vec assignment. Three baseline probes at first/middle/final drops all show capacity8 and changed pointer versus native capacity4/original pointer.
ownership_token: Consume the original LinearVector into a private ownership token. Do not implement Deref, Index, slice, iterator, AsRef, or mutable vector access. Checked extraction returns the vector only when all registered original slots are known live.

Reuse existing constructor/unpublished-tail relocation ownership while the source remains fully valid. A relocation panic keeps the token original valid and preserves native leaked replacement prefix semantics.

After full replacement construction, retain that complete vector in ManuallyDrop and convert original allocation without relocation into ManuallyDrop<Vec<MaybeUninit<T>>>. This raw representation is valid even with dead slots and cannot accidentally run T destructors.

Immediately before each original drop_in_place, advance dead_end. A throwing destructor therefore leaves [0,dead_end) dead and [dead_end,size) live. Track reconstructed prefix independently so repair panic leaves [repaired,dead_end) dead.

During interruption, expose only logical size/capacity, liveness progress, and raw pointers. No safe reference covers an uninitialized slot. Methods that require a valid vector reject this state before accessing elements.

Explicit repair constructs into tracked dead slots in ascending order; publish each repaired lifetime only after successful construction. When all holes are filled, reconstitute Vec<T> from the same allocation and permit extraction. Repair performs no silent cleanup of abandoned replacement objects.

An interrupted token dropped without repair intentionally forgets both raw original allocation/live suffix and completed replacement. This preserves memory safety and does not invent native automatic destruction/free of invalid registered slots. A valid token drops its valid original normally; abandoned replacement remains deliberately forgotten.

Test-only ownership extraction reclaims the abandoned replacement after native observations. It is not a production hook or automatic recovery policy. Test teardown repairs every original hole before normal original destruction.

A successful destruction loop leaves no old live slots, releases original allocation without T Drop, then publishes the complete replacement. Ordinary safe reserve behavior and its existing destructor-panic tests remain unchanged.
lifetime_provenance_contract: Raw storage conversion must preserve allocator, capacity, alignment and allocation provenance. Vec<T> and Vec<MaybeUninit<T>> have identical T element layout/alignment; no raw allocation is freed twice or reconstructed with wrong capacity.

Destruction takes place at actual original slot addresses. No safe slice or &T can span a dead slot. No &mut reference to a T survives its drop_in_place; each raw slot pointer is derived for its one lifetime operation.
For a destructor panic Rust field cleanup ends the entire T lifetime; the throwing slot must never be considered still live. A failed repair callback returns no T and writes no slot.

Callbacks receiving &mut T must leave their source valid on unwind; safe callback signatures enforce ordinary Rust validity. Address-dependent placement construction and callback-time aliases of the original C++ receiver remain separate unsupported domains.

Token metadata observation is independent of safe element access. Native destructor callback metadata is recorded directly; Rust tests must not fabricate aliased references to the exclusively borrowed token/vector just to reproduce that observation.

Panic payload is propagated unchanged. No production catch/resume is needed for progress: counters advance before destruction and after successful repair. Borrowed lifetimes, covariance, auto-traits and zero-sized Rust safety need separate compiler/Miri checks.

Public reserve entry is explicitly unsafe: no live references may alias original slots or owned payload lifetimes being ended, and callbacks may not alias the exclusively borrowed token. The token still statically blocks all safe reads/extraction/drop of dead values.
required_tests: Native17 cases/59 rows including original-slot destructor addresses and metadata, exact live suffix/replacement state, explicit repair, and first/middle/final repair failures.
Public token extraction and repeated growth reject dead state without reading/dropping slots. Compile-fail probes prove absence of safe slice/index/Deref access.
Strict Miri validates interrupted and partially repaired lifetimes/provenance, exact panic payload, empty/ZST, owned/borrowed domains, and typed teardown without ignore-leaks.
Normal safe reserve original destructor behavior remains independently tested. All49 legacy declarations remain unchanged and green.
out_of_scope: Shrink/Clear/destructive Erase reuse until their distinct publication order is audited.
Automatic recovery of arbitrary native invalid state, OOM/allocator exceptions, generalized placement/alias/ABI parity.
